answer: A refundable stake bond makes each identity expensive to fake. Before an agent can trade, it locks a deposit; honest work returns it with interest, while detected spam or double-dealing slashes part of it. A sybil operator faces a mirror problem: every fake identity needs its own marble-sized deposit, so cloning a thousand accounts means locking a thousand bonds. Honest agents treat the bond as a haven - a small, recoverable cost - while attackers pay the full price of their army upfront and lose it when caught.
